audits.title: 505. Use of CLABSI Prevention Bundle Audits to Decrease CLABSI Rates in COVID Positive ICU Patients in an Acute Care Hospital in New York City During the COVID-19 Epidemic
audits.setting: COVID ICUs, Mount Sinai Beth Israel, 220-bed acute care hospital, New York

cycle1.result: Bundle compliance 13%; ICU CLABSI 3.3 per 1,000 central line days (April-May).

audits.intervention: Infusion nurses performed daily intensive central line maintenance rounds for a month, educating ICU nurses and emailing daily reports to nursing leadership.

cycle2.result: Bundle compliance 88%; CLABSI rate fell to 0.

audits.other_findings: Baseline problems included undated, bloody or non-intact dressings, misplaced CHG discs and missing alcohol caps.
audits.citation: Moss M, Ehni J, Herbison I, Rabii K, Koepsell C, Devries E, et al.. 505. Use of CLABSI Prevention Bundle Audits to Decrease CLABSI Rates in COVID Positive ICU Patients in an Acute Care Hospital in New York City During the COVID-19 Epidemic. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2020;7(Suppl 1):S318-S319.

audits.title: A statewide quality improvement collaborative to reduce neonatal central line-associated blood stream infections.
audits.setting: 13 regional neonatal intensive care units, statewide collaborative, California
audits.intervention: Quality improvement collaborative: leadership commitment, potentially best practices, collaborative processes, audit and feedback tools and QI techniques.

audits.title: Using a combined nursing and medical approach to reduce the incidence of central line associated bacteraemia in a New Zealand critical care unit: a clinical audit.
audits.standard: Median central line associated bacteraemia rate of zero

cycle1.result: Mean CLAB rate 6.43 per 1000 catheter days (range 0-12.30, median 6.3).

audits.intervention: Combined nursing and medical approach with sequential insertion, maintenance and high-risk patient central line bundles

cycle2.result: Insertion bundle reduced mean CLAB rate to 1.50 per 1000 catheter days (median 0, p=.02); maintenance and high-risk bundles sustained median of zero over 12 months.

audits.citation: Hocking C, Pirret AM. Using a combined nursing and medical approach to reduce the incidence of central line associated bacteraemia in a New Zealand critical care unit: a clinical audit. Intensive Crit Care Nurs. 2013;29(3):137-146. doi:10.1016/j.iccn.2012.11.004. PMID: 23290605.

audits.title: A multicenter quasi-experimental study: impact of a central line infection control program using auditing and performance feedback in five Belgian intensive care units.
audits.standard: Compliance with five central venous catheter care processes and CLABSI rate
audits.setting: Five adult ICUs (53 beds) in two tertiary hospitals
audits.intervention: External monitoring of five CVC care processes by a trained research nurse with monthly meetings and feedback reports of performance indicators to ICU staff.

cycle2.period: Up to September 2012 (phase 2 intervention and phase 3)
cycle2.result: CLABSI rate 1.81 (0.46-3.17) per 1,000 CVC-days in phase 2, IRR 0.49 (0.24-0.98, p = 0.043); significantly improved compliance for hand hygiene, CVC handling and CVC dressing.

audits.other_findings: Better response in hospital A, where nurse attendance at monthly meetings was significantly higher.
audits.citation: Cherifi S, Gerard M, Arias S, Byl B. A multicenter quasi-experimental study: impact of a central line infection control program using auditing and performance feedback in five Belgian intensive care units. Antimicrob Resist Infect Control. 2013;2(1):33. doi:10.1186/2047-2994-2-33. PMID: 24308851.

audits.title: Impact of personalized report cards on nurses managing central lines.
audits.standard: Established guidelines for central line management (visual and documentation audits)
audits.setting: 715-bed acute community hospital system, two campuses, Naples, Florida; 14 nursing units

cycle1.result: 113 lines (19.2%) failed the visual audit; 628 CLABSI contributing factors identified.

audits.intervention: Confidential unit case reports to nurse managers and personalised report cards to 487 bedside nurses.

cycle2.result: Frequency of CLABSI contributing factors decreased over time (ρ = -0.12, P = .003).

audits.other_findings: Change was measured over the same period as the feedback rather than as a separate re-audit.
audits.citation: Morrison T, Raffaele J, Brennaman L. Impact of personalized report cards on nurses managing central lines. Am J Infect Control. 2017;45(1):24-28. doi:10.1016/j.ajic.2016.09.020. PMID: 28065330.

audits.title: Minimizing central line-associated bloodstream infections in a high-acuity liver transplant intensive care unit.
audits.standard: Central venous catheter care process measures (complete compliance) and CLABSI rate per 1,000 CVC days
audits.setting: Liver transplant intensive care unit, UCLA Ronald Reagan Medical Center

cycle1.result: Complete compliance with process measures 25%; CLABSI rate 4.2 per 1,000 CVC days.

audits.intervention: 14 interventions via Lean and PDSA cycles: infection prevention, care standardisation, team-based monitoring, audit and feedback and education.

cycle2.result: Complete compliance 67%; CLABSI rate 1.8 per 1,000 CVC days (61.2% annual reduction).

audits.citation: Russell TA, Fritschel E, Do J, Donovan M, Keckeisen M, Agopian VG, et al.. Minimizing central line-associated bloodstream infections in a high-acuity liver transplant intensive care unit. Am J Infect Control. 2019;47(3):305-312. doi:10.1016/j.ajic.2018.08.006. PMID: 30333081.

audits.title: Multi-level Intervention Program - A Quality Improvement Initiative to Decrease Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in the Pediatric Acute and Hematology/Oncology Units.
audits.setting: Paediatric acute care and haematology-oncology units, UCLA Mattel Children's Hospital; quaternary setting

cycle1.result: 41 hospital-acquired CLABSIs; quarterly rates 2.8-6.6/1,000 catheter days (acute care) and 2.1-4.3/1,000 (haematology-oncology).

audits.intervention: Multi-level intervention programme led by a Bug Buster Committee.

cycle2.result: Adherence 90% to 100% across intervention features; CLABSIs fell to 9 incidents.

audits.other_findings: Lowest adherence was for personal protective equipment, with poor parent and family adherence.

audits.title: Eliminating Central Line Associated Bloodstream Infections in Pediatric Oncology Patients: A Quality Improvement Effort.
audits.standard: SMART aim to reduce CLABSI by 50% from 1.89 to below 0.9 per 1000 central line days by 31 December 2021
audits.setting: Paediatric haematology/oncology, St Louis Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: CLABSI rate 1.89/1000 central line days (11 primary CLABSI); average 30 days between events.

audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary team, key driver diagram and PDSA cycles, including direct-observation audits of line care tasks.

cycle2.result: CLABSI rate 0.73/1000 central line days (4 primary CLABSI); average 73 days between events.

audits.other_findings: Direct observation audits gave more accurate compliance assessment than documentation audits; 542 CLABSI-free days achieved.
audits.citation: Willis DN, Looper K, Malone RA, Ricken B, Slater A, Fuller A, et al.. Eliminating Central Line Associated Bloodstream Infections in Pediatric Oncology Patients: A Quality Improvement Effort. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2023;8(3):e660. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000660. PMID: 37250614.

audits.title: Central venous catheter care and the healthcare-environment interface: outcomes of a quality improvement initiative in a resource-constrained ICU.
audits.standard: Central venous catheter insertion and maintenance bundle checklists
audits.setting: Emergency surgical ICU, Zagazig University Hospital

cycle1.result: Maintenance bundle compliance 39.5%; insertion compliance 62.5%; CLABSI 7.56 ± 2.26 per 1,000 CVC days.

audits.intervention: Standardised CLABSI definitions, insertion and maintenance checklists with daily audits, targeted staff education, and a multidisciplinary CLABSI working group for monitoring and feedback (PDSA cycles).

cycle2.result: Maintenance compliance 59.7% (p = 0.01); insertion compliance 72% (p = 0.6); CLABSI 6.97 ± 1.31 per 1,000 CVC days (-13.4%).

audits.other_findings: 1,370 patients and 2,277 CVC days in total; device utilisation ratio fell from 2.21 to 0.98 (p = 0.02); hand hygiene correlated strongly with CLABSI rates.
audits.citation: El-Sokkary RH, Negm EM, ElNaser FA, Soliman AZM, Afifi AHM, Morsi SSA, et al.. Central venous catheter care and the healthcare-environment interface: outcomes of a quality improvement initiative in a resource-constrained ICU. Front Public Health. 2025;13:1713370. doi:10.3389/fpubh.2025.1713370. PMID: 41458411.

audits.title: Strength in numbers: Utilization of an innovative electronic audit to enhance the completion of central line maintenance audits.
audits.standard: Central line maintenance bundle for central line-associated bloodstream infection prevention
audits.setting: Large children's hospital (Duke Children's Hospital and Health Center)

cycle1.result: Average 36 bundle audits per month; average bundle compliance score 76.3%.

audits.intervention: Electronic real-time audit data entry by CLABSI prevention champions, feeding an electronic dashboard so units could see their performance.

cycle2.result: Average 64 audits per month (P = .001); average compliance score 89.3% (P = .001).

audits.other_findings: Special cause variation was seen on statistical process control charts.

audits.title: Sustained decline in central line-associated bloodstream infections following a multifaceted intervention in a pediatric referral hospital in Vietnam.
audits.standard: CLABSI prevention bundle compliance; CLABSI per 1000 central line-days
audits.setting: Six intensive care units, Vietnam National Children's Hospital, Hanoi
audits.intervention: CLABSI prevention bundle (2020-2021), then compliance monitoring with checklists and data-driven audit and feedback (2021-2024).

cycle2.result: CLABSI rate 0.9 per 1000 central line-days (84.5% reduction); full bundle compliance rose from 84.6% in 2021 to 93.1% in 2024.

audits.other_findings: 12 189 central line insertions observed; overall bundle compliance 89.7%.

audits.title: Decreasing Central Line-associated Bloodstream Infections Through Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.standard: Hand hygiene and CLABSI care bundle protocols (audited as process indicators)
audits.setting: Tertiary-care neonatal intensive care unit, St John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore

cycle1.period: June 2015 to August 2015 (first 3 months of June 2015 to August 2016 study)
cycle1.result: Baseline CLABSI rate 31.7 per 1000 line-days; bloodstream infections 7.3 per 1000 patient-days; mortality 2.9%.

audits.intervention: QI team formed; measures to strengthen hand hygiene and central line bundle care, reinforced through multiple PDSA cycles with audits.

cycle2.result: CLABSI 3.5 per 1000 line-days (89% reduction); bloodstream infections 2.3 per 1000 patient-days; mortality 1.7%.

audits.other_findings: Compliance with hand hygiene and CLABSI protocols improved significantly (figures not given in the abstract).
audits.citation: Balla KC, Rao SP, Arul C, Shashidhar A, Prashantha YN, Nagaraj S, et al.. Decreasing Central Line-associated Bloodstream Infections Through Quality Improvement Initiative. Indian Pediatr. 2018;55(9):753-756. doi:10.1007/s13312-018-1374-5. PMID: 30345978.

audits.title: Transforming central line associated blood stream infection prevention in neonates: Results from a multimodal quality improvement initiative.
audits.standard: Target of 50% reduction in CLABSI rates within 12 months, sustained for a further 18 months
audits.setting: Level-3 teaching neonatal intensive care unit

cycle1.result: Baseline CLABSI rate 6.4 per 1000 central line days

audits.intervention: Multimodal bundle: strengthened hand hygiene, updated CLABSI prevention bundles, revised environmental cleaning protocols, regular audits of line insertion and maintenance, and structured nursing education, refined over multiple PDSA cycles

cycle2.result: CLABSI rate 1.1 per 1000 central line days (83% reduction)

audits.other_findings: During the 18-month sustainability phase rates stayed low at 0.96 per 1000 central line days; hand hygiene compliance, bundle adherence and nursing education coverage improved significantly.
audits.citation: Pillai A, Kabra N, Nayak A, Bhanushali M, Balasubramanian H, Shivananda S. Transforming central line associated blood stream infection prevention in neonates: Results from a multimodal quality improvement initiative. World J Clin Pediatr. 2026;15(3):118413. doi:10.5409/wjcp.118413. PMID: 42625981.
